candidates.reason: The route, API contract, authorized traffic, and advisory scanner signal all point to a webhook test-delivery path that needs an outbound destination boundary review.
candidates.broken_invariant: Webhook test deliveries must restrict outbound requests to approved customer-controlled destinations and deny internal network targets.
candidates.impact_rationale: A missing egress boundary could let an authorized user trigger server-side requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
candidates.repair_guidance: Validate webhook destinations with an allowlist or strict denylist for private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges before dispatching the test request.
candidates.regression_test: Add a local non-destructive egress-policy test proving private, loopback, link-local, and metadata URLs are rejected before outbound dispatch.
evidence_needed: Authorized local code path proving the handler reaches the outbound webhook dispatcher.
OpenAPI route metadata for the webhook test-delivery endpoint.
Redacted HAR route metadata showing the endpoint exists in authorized traffic.
Advisory scanner signal tied to the same route, treated only as a prioritization hint.
false_positive_checks: Does URL validation reject private, loopback, link-local, and metadata address ranges before dispatch?
Does DNS resolution happen inside a protected resolver that prevents rebinding to internal addresses?
Is the feature limited to pre-verified webhook destinations that the caller cannot freely edit?
safe_validation_plan: Review only local code and sanitized route metadata before any validation.
Use local unit fixtures for blocked URL categories without network dispatch.
Keep any report draft submission-blocked until human evidence and redaction review.

report_readiness.next_allowed_action: Review egress-boundary evidence, refutation checks, repair guidance, and safety blockers before exporting a report preview.
